sources.title: Generating Synthetic Multivariate Data with Copulas
sources.snippet: Photo by May on Unsplash A Copula is a multivariate cumulative distribution function where the marginal probability distribution of each variable is uniform on the interval [0,1]. But what exactly does this mean?

sources.title: Copula (statistics) - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Copula (statistics) In probability theory and statistics, a copula is a multivariate cumulative distribution function for which the marginal probability distribution of each variable is uniform on the interval [0, 1]. Copulas are used to describe / model the dependence (inter-correlation) between random variables. [1]

sources.title: The Bivariate Normal Copula Christian Meyer*† November 26, 2024
sources.snippet: Abstract We collect well known and less known facts about the bivariate normal distribution and translate them into copula language. In addition, we prove a very general formula for the bivariate normal copula, we compute Gini's gamma, and we provide improved bounds and approximations on the diagonal.
